trajectory_summary: The call moved smoothly through verify and bill capture with a cooperative customer, but energy leaked during a messy scheduling negotiation where the rep contradicted himself on availability and let the customer do the anchoring. It closed on a booked date/time with the bill in hand, but the button-up lacked the standard hour-block and fairness-handshake elements.

observed_outcome.quote: I can do Monday, the twentieth, at 09:30.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day and time were agreed by the customer and confirmed by the rep; the wife was identified as co-owner at 01:29 but never explicitly confirmed for the appointment.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: Rep captured the $1,100-$1,300 bill and reacted with surprise ("Oh, wow. Really? It's that high?") but never explicitly reused the number to frame the appointment or reinforce urgency; the flip should have landed around 09:49 when confirming the appointment.

bill_document_audit.ask_quote: So you can get that over to me either text or email, whichever one works better for you.
bill_document_audit.reasoning: The rep asked for the bill by email/text and the customer sent it during the call; the rep confirmed receipt at 09:49.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: "Just energy costs" was captured as the interest reason but never referenced again when booking or confirming the appointment.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: it looks like we'll have someone in your area as soon as tomorrow or Thursday, if any of those days would work good for you.
primary_coaching_focus.why: Five rounds of offer-and-retract on days/times let the customer drive the booking and included two self-corrected errors, risking credibility and no-show if the closer follows an unclear brief.
